headline: 23 contracts catalogued across Ethereum and Gnosis; 9 re-verified from address_book, 14 newly surfaced from GitHub docs and Etherscan labels; multi-chain deployments (BSC, Arbitrum, Polygon, Optimism, Avalanche, EthereumClassic) not resolved to addresses this run.

Deployment artifacts (run-latest.json, deployments/*.json) not directly fetched; address list sourced from docs/general/tornado-cash-smart-contracts.md snippet. No pinned commit SHA obtained.

Gnosis multisig 0x1f727de610030a88863d7da45bdea4eb84655b52 carried forward from address_book. D6: InstanceRegistry (0xB20c66C4DE72433F3cE747b58B86830c459CA911) and RelayerRegistry (0x58E8dCC13BE9780fC42E8723D8EaD4CF46943dF2) are factory-like registries. No factory enumeration call made this run — factory addresses recorded, enumeration deferred.
D7: Role taxonomy applied to all admin_addresses[] entries using controlled vocabulary: governor, token, router, multisig, other, factory, vault, pool.

D8: All admin_addresses[] entries trace to fetched defipunkd surfacer pages or search-returned GitHub docs/Etherscan snippets. Safe master copy 0x34CfAC646f301356fAa8B21e94227e3583Fe3F5F surfaced only via defipunkd surfacer crawl manifest; not independently confirmed — recorded in unknowns[] rather than admin_addresses.

rationale.verdict: Discovery run walked the defipunkd surfacer pages for all 9 address_book entries, search-retrieved the tornadocash/docs GitHub smart-contracts page and Etherscan labels, cataloguing 23 contracts on Ethereum and Gnosis. Six additional chains (BSC, Arbitrum, Polygon, Optimism, Avalanche, EthereumClassic) produced zero addresses due to exhausted fetch/search budget; audit PDF fetch failed due to IPNS website inaccessibility.

protocol_metadata.about: Tornado Cash is a non-custodial, zkSNARK-based cryptocurrency privacy protocol deployed across multiple EVM chains. Users deposit fixed denominations of ETH or ERC-20 tokens (or arbitrary amounts via Tornado Cash Nova on Gnosis Chain) and later withdraw to a fresh address with no on-chain link to the deposit, using zero-knowledge proofs to preserve privacy. The core pool contracts are immutable and cannot be upgraded or paused by anyone; peripheral contracts (router, relayer registry, fee manager, instance registry, staking rewards) are upgradeable and governed by the TORN-token DAO. The protocol was sanctioned by the US Treasury in August 2022 but those sanctions were partially overturned by a US federal appeals court in November 2024.
